I rarely leave negative reviews, but I feel other pet owners should know about my experience.

We scheduled an appointment because our 8-year-old Labrador needed a refill of her pain medication and an antibiotic after having a large mass removed while we were home on leave in Indiana. We have been doing her wound care ourselves for several weeks, so we brought all of our own bandaging supplies specifically because we know this clinic charges a significant amount for bandage changes.

Our appointment was at 3:00 p.m., but we weren’t called back until 3:22 p.m. The veterinary technician spent about five minutes with us while we explained everything about our dog’s surgery, current medications, wound care, and even showed him photos. He told us he would relay all of the information to the veterinarian.

About 20 minutes later, the veterinarian came into the room and, unfortunately, it became obvious that none of the information had been passed along. We had to repeat everything from the beginning.

During the exam, I mentioned that I thought our dog might have an ear infection. The veterinarian agreed and offered medication, which I approved.

The biggest issue came at checkout. I was surprised to see charges for services that were never discussed with me beforehand:

* A bandage charge of $38.95, even though we brought our own bandaging supplies.
* An ear cleaning charge of $42.95, which I was never told would be performed or billed separately.
* A charge of $35.57 to apply the ear medication, in addition to the cleaning.
* Ironically, the medications we actually came in for totaled only $32.85.

Including the office visit, my total bill came to $232.32 for what I believed was primarily a medication refill appointment.

My concern isn’t simply the total cost, it’s the lack of transparency. If additional procedures are going to be performed and billed separately, clients should be informed beforehand so they can make an informed decision. Finding out only after arriving at the checkout counter is frustrating and disappointing.

To make matters worse, the cleanliness of the clinic was concerning. The facility appeared dirty from the floors to the ceiling. I’ve attached a photo of the ceiling, along with my invoice, so others can judge for themselves.

As pet owners, we trust veterinary clinics to communicate clearly, be transparent about costs, and provide a clean environment for our animals. Unfortunately, this experience fell well short of those expectations. We will not be back.

I am posting this follow up review of a procedure that was done to my dog around 7 months ago. Initially I needed a simple tooth extracted for a fracture, long story short I was tricked into getting a cleaning done as well that I never wanted or asked for but still had to pay since the procedure was done. The wording for the cleaning was not listed in plain terms and was a descriptive wording that I thought was for the tooth extraction. Looking not only past that they didn’t even get my dogs full tooth out. After infection due to a terribly done surgery we took our dog to a different veterinary hospital, that showed us that more than half the tooth was left in his mouth, and specifically stated “they didn’t even do an extraction, his whole root is still in there” leading to a very uncomfortable time for my dog for the past 6 months, displaying signs of pain when eating, licking etc. Due to the lack of good procedure the tooth next to his supposedly extracted one had to be removed as well due to the damage of them operating on the broken tooth from the first surgery. This vet clinic already failed my dog once so I was not going to have them put him in more pain along with the possibility of paying for more add ons I never asked for or just plain giving them more money for not doing their job. Photos for evidence, x ray shows the entire root of my dogs tooth left behind along with pieces of his normally exposed tooth.
Hopefully this vet clinic will take responsibility and reach out to us regarding this issues and malpractice.
I would highly encourage folks to review every little detail and word on their invoice before getting tricked into paying for stuff you didn’t ask for and pray that when you take your pets to this hospital that you are truly getting what you paid for. In our case, we did NOT at all get what we paid for and had to pay twice just to have our dog taken care of properly which should have happened in the first place.

I was charged for a dental cleaning I never wanted. My dog fractured his tooth playing fetch and when I went to my original vet they gave me an estimate but was not able to see my dog for two weeks. Due to the pain he was in I went to St. Francis because my other dog had been seen there. They said they could get my dog in the following day, conduct an exam and extract the tooth. At no point did I ask for a dental cleaning. When I received the invoice it showed the various charges and one large charge for “k9 dental prophy grade 1-2 51lbs”. This estimate they gave was almost the exact same as my other vet so I figured this was normal. When I took him in the next day there was no mention of a cleaning only words used was “dental” and “tooth extraction”. A normal person who has no understanding of the Vetinarian world interprets this most likely as the same thing, dental being an overall term for teeth procedures. Well after the procedure was done I submitted an insurance claim to my pet insurance, I was only reimbursed 25 percent because the rest of the charge fell under “wellness”.  I then figure out that the term was for a dental cleaning. I called to confront them about this and I was told I signed the invoice so I accepted all charges.

There are multiple issues with this:

1.) I never asked for a dental cleaning so it should have never been added.
2.) There should be a in person break down that explains things like this so someone doesn’t get scammed. Looking over the invoice it looked to be a bunch of terms involving extraction of a tooth.
3.) They tried to tell me this was disgusted but at no point because I would have remembered and told them not to conduct the cleaning. Only terms used in discussion of the procedure was dental and extraction. To be exact before I handed him to the vet the phrase used was “Dental with extraction”. To me that sounds like he is going in for a dental procedure for an extraction.

Make sure you look at every charge on an invoice because they will put something in there you don’t want or need.
